source.publication: 2025 Form CT-1040 Instructions (Rev. 12/25) and Form CT-1040
source.section: PDF pages 24-25, Pension and Annuity Worksheet Lines 1-4 and Phase-Out Table (single, 75,000-77,499: .85); PDF pages 19-23, Tax Calculation Schedule Lines 1-10 with Table A, Table B, Tables C-D and Table E; Form CT-1040 Lines 1-6

worked: Federal AGI = wages 35,000.00 + private pension 40,000.00 = 75,000.00. Federal taxable income = 75,000.00 - 15,750.00 standard deduction = 59,250.00 (given, not tested; federal senior deduction ignored). CT-1040 Line 1 federal AGI 75,000.00; Line 2 additions 0.00 (Schedule 1 Lines 31-37: none apply); Line 3 = 75,000.00. Schedule 1 Line 48b pension and annuity (Line 5b part): Phase-Out Table: federal AGI 75,000.00 is 75,000.00 or more, decimal 0.85; 40,000.00 x 0.85 = 34,000.00 -> 34,000.00. Schedule 1 Line 50 total subtractions = 34,000.00; CT-1040 Line 4 = 34,000.00. CT-1040 Line 5 Connecticut AGI = 75,000.00 - 34,000.00 = 41,000.00. Tax Calculation Schedule Line 1 = 41,000.00; Line 2 Table A: Connecticut AGI 41,000.00 is more than 40,000.00, exemption 4,000.00; Line 3 taxable income = 41,000.00 - 4,000.00 = 37,000.00. Line 4 Table B (Single or Married Filing Separately schedule) on 37,000.00: 10,000.00 x 0.02 + 27,000.00 x 0.045 = 200.00 + 1,215.00 = 1,415.00. Line 5 Table C 0.00 (Connecticut AGI 41,000.00 is not more than 56,500.00); Line 6 Table D 0.00 (not more than 105,000.00); Line 7 = 1,415.00. Line 8 Table E decimal 0.10 (Connecticut AGI 41,000.00 is in the band more than 33,300.00); Line 9 = 1,415.00 x 0.10 = 141.50. Line 10 Connecticut income tax = 1,415.00 - 141.50 = 1,273.50 (CT-1040 Line 6). No other credits (property tax credit not claimed: no property tax in the inputs, and not modelled). Note: Federal AGI exactly 75,000 is '75,000 or more', so the worksheet is completed and the .85 decimal applies.
